findings.quote: Only a strong push from a concentrated positive charge could turn a heavy, fast alpha particle through a large angle.
findings.problem: This 'only' statement fails a known exception, and the lesson presents it as Rutherford's 1911 reasoning. A concentrated negative charge would also turn an alpha particle through large angles, by a strong pull instead of a push. Rutherford's 1911 paper says its main results are the same whether the central charge is positive or negative. He took it as positive only for convenience and said the sign was not yet settled. The scattering showed that the charge and mass are concentrated. It did not show the sign of the charge. This is the evidence-to-inference skill that the lesson's goal and Example #4 teach. The sentence teaches the student to claim more than the evidence shows.
findings.source: E. Rutherford, 'The Scattering of alpha and beta Particles by Matter and the Structure of the Atom', Philosophical Magazine 21 (1911): 'the main deductions from the theory are independent of whether the central charge is supposed to be positive or negative. For convenience, the sign will be assumed to be positive' (text at chemteam.info/Chem-History/Rutherford-1911/Rutherford-1911.html); March 1911 abstract: 'It has not yet been found possible to settle this question of sign with certainty'; checklist B01; reader-rules boundary test

findings.problem: The round-2 finding is still open. The cathode-ray paragraph that starts here has six sentences. The isotope paragraph that starts 'This contradicts Dalton's claim that all atoms of one element have the same mass.' has five, and so do several others, such as the Bohr photon paragraph and the quantum-mechanics paragraph. Paragraphs should be one to three short sentences.

findings.quote: It does **not** correctly describe atoms with many electrons.
findings.problem: This sentence uses bold to stress the word 'not'. The guide keeps bold for a key term the first time it is defined, and it uses italics, rarely, for light stress. The line was rewritten in this round, so new or edited content must fix this Minor.
